summary: Connect your Todoist account through Composio's managed OAuth app and read your active (incomplete) tasks with TODOIST_GET_ALL_TASKS via a Composio session.

overview.reason: Composio provides the managed Todoist OAuth app, so no provider app registration or client secret is needed; you only connect your own Todoist account.
overview.agentCan: Install the SDK, write and run the session script, and call TODOIST_GET_ALL_TASKS once a connection exists.
overview.youHandle: Create a Composio account/API key, open the Connect Link, log in to Todoist, and review/approve the consent screen. This is a private test setup, not approval for external users.

effort.basis: Assumes an existing Composio account/API key and a Todoist account with at least one task; no provider app registration is needed.

prerequisites.title: Composio account with an API key
prerequisites.detail: Composio manages the Todoist OAuth app (toolkit TODOIST, auth OAUTH2), so you do not register your own Todoist OAuth app.

permissions.name: Todoist OAuth via Composio-managed app
permissions.reason: Reading your active tasks requires an authenticated Todoist connection; Composio hosts the OAuth app and stores/refreshes tokens.

permissions.name: Composio API key
permissions.reason: Authenticates SDK calls to Composio's backend; pass it explicitly or via the documented COMPOSIO_API_KEY fallback.

steps.title: Install the Composio SDK
steps.detail: The composio package provides the Composio class and session APIs used throughout this guide.
steps.recovery: If install fails, check your Python/pip environment and retry; no Composio account changes are involved.
instructions: Run: pip install composio
Confirm the install completes without errors.

steps.title: Construct the SDK client with your API key
steps.action: Construct the SDK client with your API key
steps.detail: Source 13 documents that omitting apiKey falls back to the COMPOSIO_API_KEY environment variable (then the CLI-stored key). Passing it explicitly is also supported; either way, keep the real key out of chat and source control.
steps.successCheck: The Composio instance constructs without an API-key error.
steps.recovery: If calls return 401, verify the key is valid in the Composio dashboard and that it was passed or set in COMPOSIO_API_KEY.
instructions: Obtain your Composio API key from your Composio dashboard (user input).
In your script: import os; from composio import Composio
composio = Composio(api_key=os.environ["COMPOSIO_API_KEY"])  # explicit pass; omitting api_key also falls back to COMPOSIO_API_KEY
Never paste the real key into chat or committed code.

steps.title: Create a Composio session
steps.detail: Sessions scope tool access and connected accounts to one user ID; use a stable identifier, not 'default' in production.
steps.successCheck: A session object is returned without error.
steps.recovery: If creation fails, check the API key and that the SDK version supports composio.create(user_id=...).
instructions: session = composio.create(user_id="user_123")  # replace user_123 with your stable user ID
print(session)

steps.title: Generate the Todoist Connect Link
steps.detail: session.authorize('todoist') starts a hosted authorization flow using Composio's managed OAuth app; no client ID or secret from you.
steps.recovery: If authorize fails, confirm the TODOIST toolkit is available to your project and your API key has session permissions.
instructions: connection_request = session.authorize("todoist")
print(connection_request.redirect_url)  # a https://connect.composio.dev/link/... URL

steps.title: Connect your Todoist account
steps.action: Open the Connect Link and approve consent
steps.detail: Composio hosts the OAuth consent; the exact scopes Composio's managed Todoist app requests are not documented in the sources, so review the consent screen before approving.
steps.successCheck: The browser shows the connection completed.
steps.recovery: If you close the link without completing, the connection stays INITIATED until it expires; call session.authorize('todoist') again for a fresh link.
instructions: Open the printed redirect_url in a browser (user input).
Log in to Todoist if prompted.
Review the permissions shown on the consent screen and approve them.

steps.title: Wait for the connection to become active
steps.detail: wait_for_connection polls until authentication completes; the 60000 ms argument is a polling timeout, not an approval waiting period.
steps.successCheck: A connected account ID is printed.
steps.recovery: On timeout while the user is still authenticating, call wait_for_connection again or re-run authorize for a new link.
instructions: connected_account = connection_request.wait_for_connection(60000)
print(connected_account.id)

steps.title: Read your active tasks
steps.detail: TODOIST_GET_ALL_TASKS returns only incomplete (active) tasks; completed tasks need a different tool. No filter returns all active tasks.
steps.successCheck: result.result_type == 'completed' and result.data contains your task list.
steps.recovery: A 400 from a filter means invalid terms; with no filter this should not occur. If execution fails, check the connection is ACTIVE and retry.
instructions: result = session.execute("TODOIST_GET_ALL_TASKS", arguments={})
if result.result_type == "failed": raise RuntimeError(result.error or f"Tool execution failed (log ID: {result.log_id})")
print(result.data)

steps.title: Confirm this stays a private test
steps.action: Launch check for this test setup
steps.detail: No distribution or external-user approval is part of this request; Composio production suitability, branding and workspace-admin approval were not evaluated in the sources.
steps.successCheck: You have explicitly confirmed this is a single-user test with no external distribution.
steps.recovery: If you later need external users, re-check Composio production guidance before distributing.
instructions: Do not share the Connect Link or connected account with other users.
Note that no evidence in the sources covers production rollout or external-user approval for this setup.

blockers.title: Managed Todoist scopes not published
blockers.detail: The Composio-managed Todoist OAuth app's granted scopes are not documented in the supplied sources, so read access cannot be pre-verified; the consent screen at connection time is the authoritative check.

agentBrief: Task: read active Todoist tasks via Composio-managed OAuth (test audience). Confirmed: Todoist toolkit TODOIST, auth OAUTH2, Composio-managed OAuth available (https://docs.composio.dev/toolkits/todoist). Route: Python SDK sessions. Install composio, construct Composio(api_key=...) — source 13 documents that omitting apiKey falls back to the COMPOSIO_API_KEY environment variable, so either explicit passing or the env var works. Then composio.create(user_id), session.authorize('todoist') returns redirect_url for the user to open and consent; wait_for_connection polls until active (60000 ms is a polling timeout, not an approval wait). Then session.execute('TODOIST_GET_ALL_TASKS', arguments={}) returns incomplete (active) tasks; check result.result_type == 'completed'. Agent can write/run this code; human must supply the Composio API key, open the Connect Link, log in to Todoist and approve consent. Gaps: Composio's managed Todoist scopes are not documented in sources (Todoist data:read exists per developer.todoist.com but managed-app scope set unconfirmed); TODOIST_GET_ALL_TASKS output schema truncated. Sources: docs.composio.dev/toolkits/todoist, docs.composio.dev/docs/authentication/manually-authenticating, docs.composio.dev/reference/authenticating-to-composio.
